reason: Fresh first-party checks eliminate three large active CPOs from the network-wide/class-wide queue: their current direct tariff cannot safely be represented as one deterministic network/class tariff.

changes.tariffModel: station/session-specific direct price with optional subscription discount
changes.tariffChannel: direct CPO app / on-site payment terminal / card; roaming separate
changes.positiveEvidence: Official live station FAQ says the customer pays the price shown in the app or on the charger before connecting; Electra+ applies -0.10 or -0.20 EUR/kWh from that price. Official 2026 overstay page adds a conditional 0.40 EUR/min fee after a 5-minute grace period only when SOC is above 80% and the station is busy, capped at 50 EUR/session.
negativeTests: 2025 Italy summer promo 0.39 EUR/kWh expired 2025-09-30 and is not current
No current first-party evidence that a single gross Italy tariff applies to all ELC EVSE
changes.blockage: Exact gross price must be mapped from station/connector/session surface; subscription discounts alone do not determine base tariff.
changes.resumeCondition: Extract deterministic station/connector -> current gross tariff from Electra public station/app/backend surface.

changes.tariffChannel: IONITY app / QR payment website / on-site contactless terminal; MSP roaming separate
changes.positiveEvidence: Current official IONITY support explicitly states direct-customer kWh price depends on tariff, subscription, country and specific station location, and may vary between locations within the same country. Exact price is shown in app, QR/payment website or terminal.
negativeTests: Country-level marketing values are insufficient because IONITY explicitly allows intra-country location variation
changes.blockage: No safe Italy-wide tariff; exact station mapping required for rankable direct price.
changes.resumeCondition: Resolve each IOY station/EVSE through IONITY app/QR/payment endpoint and retain exact location -> tariff mapping.

changes.tariffChannel: Route220 CPMS / POS / custom app; direct CPO attribution must be proven per EVSE
changes.positiveEvidence: Route220's current official CPMS description says customers/operators can set their own sales tariffs for Service Providers and manage payment by POS or custom app, so the platform itself does not establish a universal Route220 network tariff.
negativeTests: No first-party evidence of one current deterministic tariff applying to all partyId 220 EVSE
changes.blockage: Tariff is configurable by managed point/operator; partyId alone is insufficient to assign a price.
changes.resumeCondition: Map physical station/EVSE owner and exact direct/ad-hoc tariff from CPMS/public payment surface before ranking.

next: Continue unresolved network-wide/class-wide candidates by EVSE scope; do not investigate ELC/IOY/220 station-by-station until that queue is exhausted. Atlante remains last.
